nodes.label: Twin Experiment
nodes.rationale: Two identical cities run the same streets, trips and RNG seed; the only difference is the signal controller. Modelled demand cancels out of the comparison, which is why the experiment is a twin rather than a single before/after run.

nodes.label: Worst-Case Reporting
nodes.rationale: Quote the least favourable figure across validation runs, not the mean. The number you should be willing to defend is the worst one.

nodes.label: Emissions Warm-Up Artefact
nodes.rationale: For the first ten simulated minutes CO2 reads WORSE for the AI, because it completed 141 trips to the baseline's 63 and so burned more fuel doing more than twice the work. Delay and bus rows are meaningful from minute one; emissions are not.

nodes.label: Equity Block
nodes.rationale: Volunteer the tail metrics before anyone asks. p95 wait, worst wait and count waiting over five minutes would all worsen if the average were being bought by starving side streets.

nodes.label: Teleports Understate The Result
nodes.rationale: SUMO teleports vehicles deadlocked for four minutes. Fixed-time triggers it about twice as often as the AI, and teleported vehicles stop accruing delay, so the measured gap is smaller than the real one.

nodes.label: Six-Month Corridor Pilot
nodes.rationale: Instrument one corridor. Diagonal has 184 segments and the signal hardware already exists, so this is a controller software change rather than a construction project.

nodes.label: The Honest Claim
nodes.rationale: Streets and signals are real; trips are modelled because Barcelona publishes no O/D matrix. The claim is that the RELATIVE improvement between two identical cities is real.

nodes.label: Rules Over Reinforcement Learning
nodes.rationale: A transport authority has to sign it off. Every decision is explainable in one sentence and failure modes are bounded by construction. RL is phase two, once the pilot has generated field data to train on.

nodes.label: Pedestrian Demand Gap
nodes.rationale: Pedestrians are not modelled as crossing demand -- the acknowledged gap. Pedestrian phases are baked into imported signal programs and minimum green is never violated, so crossing time is preserved.
